body.content: Exploring the collinearity constraint: in a 4x3 grid + 1 center point, the dominant collinearities are (a) horizontal rows, (b) vertical columns, (c) diagonals. Breaking horizontal collinearity requires stagger; breaking vertical requires uneven column positions; breaking diagonal requires irrational offsets. The minimum non-degenerate triangle in a perturbed grid is bounded by the perturbation magnitude times the grid spacing. For 1/3 spacing and ~0.05 perturbation, minimum area ~ 0.5 * (1/3) * (0.05) ~ 0.008. This suggests perturbation alone is insufficient and stagger is essential.
body.possible_next_move: Try a 3-row configuration with 5-4-4 points and 1/3 stagger to see if larger row spacing improves the minimum beyond 0.0385.
body.why_keep_this: This calculation explains why the staggered grid (Candidate 1) outperforms perturbed grids: stagger provides O(spacing) horizontal offset rather than O(perturbation), giving minimum areas ~0.038 instead of ~0.008.
